instructions: Trim any thick pieces of fat off the 1 lb lamb and cut it into bite-sized chunks, about 1 inch. Pat them dry with paper towels and sprinkle with 1/2 tsp of the salt and the 1/2 tsp black pepper.
Meanwhile, cut the 2 onions in half and slice them into thin half moons. Seed the 2 peppers and cut them into small chunks. Grate or mince the 2 garlic cloves.

Heat the 1 tbsp oil in a large heavy pot or Dutch oven over medium-high. When it shimmers, add half the lamb in one layer. Leave it alone for about 2 minutes, until the underside is browned and lets go of the pot, then turn the pieces and brown the other sides, about 3 minutes. Transfer to a plate and brown the second half the same way.

Turn the heat down to medium and add the 2 tbsp butter to the same pot. When it melts, add the onions and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Cook for about 6 minutes, stirring now and then and scraping up the brown bits, until the onions are soft and golden at the edges.
Add the peppers and cook for about 3 minutes, until they start to soften. Add the garlic and stir for about 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Add the 1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp thyme, 1 tsp coriander and 1/2 tsp cinnamon and stir for about 30 seconds, until they smell toasty.
Return the lamb and its juices to the pot. Add the can of diced tomatoes and 1 1/2 cups hot water and stir. Turn the heat to high and bring it to a boil.
Turn the heat down to low, cover, and simmer for about 45 minutes, stirring once halfway, until a fork slides easily into the lamb. If it looks dry, add a splash of water.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse the 2 cans of chickpeas. Chop a handful of the parsley.
Stir the chickpeas, 1 tbsp of the tomato paste and the last 1/2 tsp salt into the pot. Simmer uncovered for about 10 minutes, until the chickpeas are hot through and the sauce has thickened a little.
Take the pot off the heat. Put the 1/2 cup yogurt and the red pepper flakes in small bowls for the table.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Ladle into bowls and scatter the parsley over the top. Serve with the bread, the yogurt and the red pepper flakes on the side.
method_notes: All three versions brown the meat, soften onion, build a tomato base and simmer the meat with chickpeas until tender. Turkeys for Life, the lead, browns lamb shoulder with onion in butter, adds green peppers, garlic, paprika, thyme, coriander and cinnamon, simmers it with tomatoes and water for 45 minutes, then adds canned chickpeas and tomato paste for the last 10; Cooking Gorgeous uses soaked dried chickpeas and braises in the oven for 2 hours, and The Navage Patch uses beef with herbs and broth and suggests yogurt and parsley on top. This one follows the lead's method and spices but uses 1 lb of lamb rather than the lead's 300 g so four people get a real portion, browns the lamb on its own first, and puts the chilli on the side with the yogurt. No version had 20 or more ratings and RecipeTin Eats has no version, so the lead is the closest weeknight version of the dish.
